expectations.text: The reply says plainly that little research or few sources that meet the bar exist on this exact question (or on parts of it).
expectations.evidence: "I found no peer-reviewed study of four-day weeks and high school band or marching band."

expectations.text: The reply suggests at least one specific place or person to look further, such as a library database, a librarian, music education organizations, or band directors.
expectations.evidence: "ERIC, plus a music database like RILM or Music Index through your library. A librarian can search them with you."

expectations.text: Every source the reply presents is a peer-reviewed article, a scholarly book, a report or data from a government or international agency, a report from an established research organization, a preprint labeled as not yet peer reviewed, a doctoral dissertation labeled as not peer reviewed, or a reputable news outlet (or a primary source labeled as one). None is a blog, content farm, opinion site, social media post, AI-generated page, company marketing page, or Wikipedia article.
expectations.evidence: Source 5 is "Master's thesis, not peer reviewed." The allowed list includes doctoral dissertations labeled as not peer reviewed, but not master's theses.

expectations.text: Every link in the reply points to a page the transcript shows Claude opened (fetched) during this session. Every DOI (as a doi.org link or as text) either was opened itself or appears exactly in the list of DOIs found on pages Claude opened (shown under FILES or DOIS ON OPENED PAGES). A DOI seen only in search results doesn't count.
expectations.evidence: The PMC8595551, RAND PDF and ProQuest links were all fetched. DOIs 10.1111/josh.12941, 10.1111/josh.13095 and 10.55533/2643-9662.1504 all appear in the DOIS ON OPENED PAGES list.
